title: IELTS Academic 21 - Listening Test 2 - Part 2
transcriptHtml:
LISTENING TRANSCRIPT - PART 2

💡 Audio-Track Sync: Bấm vào bất kỳ câu nào dưới đây để phát audio ngay đúng câu đó!

08:23ANNOUNCER: You will hear some recorded information for visitors to a region about history and nature walks there and about a particular visitor attraction.
08:34ANNOUNCER: First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.
08:59ANNOUNCER: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
09:07SPEAKER: Here is some information about history and nature walks in the region. They can be completed in less than a day and also be combined with a visit to Melby, a former coal mine now open to the public.
09:22SPEAKER: The Marsden Coastal Walk is suitable for all the family, as there are no strenuous climbs. The route begins at Marsden Harbour, where there are hourly ferries to and from the beautiful Hooker Island, a great place for fishing.
09:38SPEAKER: The walk covers part of the coastal path trail. As there are clear signposts all along the way, you don't even need to take a map with you.
09:48SPEAKER: At one point, the route goes inland slightly and passes a castle built in the 1400s, near to a now vanished market town. The castle's now just a pile of stones, but it's a great place to take photos, and fascinating information boards show what it once looked like.
10:07SPEAKER: If you set off early, you can be back in time for midday.
10:11SPEAKER: The Melby Heritage Walk is a great place to take photos, especially of the night sky. At certain times of the year, people come here from far and wide. They climb to the top of the valley and take pictures of the stars.
10:27SPEAKER: In the daytime, it's completely different. As you hike through the dense woods in the valley bottom, the only things you'll hear are the sound of your own footsteps.
10:38SPEAKER: At the highest point, you can stop to take in the views and those with lots of energy can climb the tower that's situated where there was once a 17th century hunting lodge. The route continues along the tops of the hills and brings you back down to the starting point, the car park at Melby coal mine.
11:02ANNOUNCER: Before you hear the rest of the recording information, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.
11:37ANNOUNCER: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.
11:45SPEAKER: Melby coal mine has been open to the public for 20 years and has won awards for its visitor experience. Many of the buildings around the mine are still standing and have been converted into display areas.
11:59SPEAKER: Firstly, there's an exhibition showing the history of the mine with many original black and white photos. To see that, you go from the car park via a covered walkway to the main visitor centre. Go through the ticket office to an area where there are lockers to leave heavy bags in and where you can borrow raincoats. Beyond that room is the exhibition.
12:24SPEAKER: There is a small bath house where miners used to wash after their shift underground. You can see that in the building directly to the north of the engine house. The boiler has gone from there now, but there are lines of tin baths on the stone floor.
12:41SPEAKER: There's a display of early mining tools from the days before mechanisation. You can find that in a small, L-shaped building in the middle of the northern boundary of the site. It's incredible to think how miners were able to use hand implements to cut through rock.
12:59SPEAKER: The vehicle shed, where you can find wagons of different sizes, along with some of the high-tech cutting machines that were in use until the mine closed, is in the southwest corner of the site and can be accessed via a covered walkway.
13:15SPEAKER: There is a field with ponies, which are always popular with children, on the northeastern boundary of the site, not approached via a covered walkway.
13:26SPEAKER: The other building to mention is the Education Centre. This is where school groups go when they visit the mine, but it's also accessible to the public as it contains a library and small gift shop. The centre is connected to the ticket office via a short section of covered walkway.
13:48ANNOUNCER: That is the end of Part 2.
13:51ANNOUNCER: You now have 30 seconds to check your answers to Part 2.

groups.title: Questions 15–20
groups.instructions:
Label the map below.
Choose SIX answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–I, next to Questions 15–20.

q11.text: What does the speaker highlight about the Marsden Coastal Walk?
options: A. It requires walkers to carry a topographical map.
B. It has clear signs along the entire route.
C. It involves several steep and challenging climbs.

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (It has clear signs along the entire route)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'As there are clear signposts all along the way, you don't even need to take a map with you.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Bài nói 'no strenuous climbs' (không có leo dốc vất vả) nên loại C; 'don't even need to take a map' nên loại A.

q12.text: Visitors who reach the castle along the coastal walk will find...
options: B. information boards depicting its past appearance
C. a functioning local market nearby

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (information boards depicting its past appearance)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'The castle's now just a pile of stones... and fascinating information boards show what it once looked like.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Lâu đài nay chỉ còn đống đá vụn ('just a pile of stones') và thị trấn chợ xưa đã biến mất ('now vanished market town').

q13.text: Why do many people visit the Melby Heritage Walk at night?
options: A. To take photographs of the night sky and stars
B. To participate in a guided evening wildlife tour
C. To experience the absolute silence of the valley

steps: • Đáp án đúng: A (To take photographs of the night sky and stars)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'especially of the night sky. At certain times of the year... They climb to the top of the valley and take pictures of the stars.'
• Từ khóa đối xứng: 'take pictures of the stars' = photographs of the night sky and stars.

q14.text: What can energetic walkers do when they reach the highest point of the walk?
options: A. Explore the remains of a 17th-century hunting lodge
B. Climb to the top of an observation tower
C. Take a rest in an indoor visitors' shelter

steps: • Đáp án đúng: B (Climb to the top of an observation tower)
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'those with lots of energy can climb the tower that's situated where there was once a 17th century hunting lodge.'
• Phân tích bẫy: Tòa nhà săn bắn thế kỷ 17 chỉ từng tồn tại ở đó trước đây ('where there was once...'), hiện tại chỉ có tháp để trèo lên.
• Đáp án đúng: F
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'go from the car park via a covered walkway to the main visitor centre. Go through the ticket office to an area where there are lockers... Beyond that room is the exhibition.'
• Đường đi: Từ Car park đi lối có mái che vào Ticket office -> qua phòng gửi đồ G -> phòng tiếp theo ngay phía sau là F.
• Đáp án đúng: B
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'in the building directly to the north of the engine house.'
• Định vị: Trên bản đồ, Engine house nằm ở phía tây. Tòa nhà nằm ngay phía bắc (bên trên) Engine house chính là B.
• Đáp án đúng: D
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'in a small, L-shaped building in the middle of the northern boundary of the site.'
• Định vị: Tòa nhà hình chữ L nhỏ nằm ngay chính giữa ranh giới phía bắc (mép trên cùng của khu đất) chính là D.
• Đáp án đúng: A
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'is in the southwest corner of the site and can be accessed via a covered walkway.'
• Định vị: Góc tây nam (dưới cùng bên trái) của khu đất có lối đi có mái che nối vào chính là tòa nhà A.
• Đáp án đúng: H
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'on the northeastern boundary of the site, not approached via a covered walkway.'
• Định vị: Khu vực rộng lớn nằm ở góc đông bắc (phía trên bên phải) không có lối đi mái che chính là H.
• Đáp án đúng: E
• Dấu hiệu transcript: 'connected to the ticket office via a short section of covered walkway.'
• Định vị: Ngay từ Ticket office có một lối đi mái che ngắn đi thẳng lên phía bắc nối vào tòa nhà hình chữ L E.
